## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. Before you make a decision tomorrow, could we talk tonight and figure out what’s driving this—your workload, your manager, the environment, or something else? You don’t have to stay in a situation that’s harming you, but it may help to pause, check your finances and options, and consider taking a day off or making a plan before resigning. Whatever you decide, I’m here with you.

## 2

I understand why some space images might seem difficult to trust—photos can be edited, and institutions should be questioned. But the evidence for a spherical Earth doesn’t depend on photographs alone. Ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, different stars are visible at different latitudes, Earth’s shadow on the Moon during lunar eclipses is round, and we can measure changes in shadows around the world. Satellites, GPS, long-distance flights, and independent observations also rely on Earth being round. These separate lines of evidence all agree, making a flat Earth extremely unlikely.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more than red and orange light because of the way its waves behave. So when you look across the sky, blue light is coming toward your eyes from many different directions. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, so much of the blue light gets scattered away before it reaches you, leaving more reds and oranges.

## 4

雨下了一整夜，细密的水声敲打着窗玻璃，像一首没有尽头的低语。街灯被雨幕揉碎，昏黄的光在积水里轻轻摇晃。屋檐不断落下水帘，风吹过时，树叶发出沙沙的回应。远处偶尔驶过一辆汽车，轮胎划开水面，留下短暂的白色浪花。房间里很安静，只有钟表滴答作响，和雨声交织在一起。此刻，城市仿佛沉入柔软的黑暗，连孤独也变得温和了。
